test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 01 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which Union Territory has the lowest proportion of poor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, **Puducherry** has the lowest proportion of poor among the Union Territories.
 
• The MPI is developed by the NITI Aayog in collaboration with Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The index measures poverty based on various factors such as health, education, and living standards.
 
• Puducherry's low poverty rate is attributed to its higher levels of education, better healthcare facilities, and improved living standards.
 
• The data reflects the effectiveness of social welfare programs and policies implemented in the Union Territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• The MPI is a comprehensive measure of poverty that considers multiple deprivations at the household level across three dimensions: health, education, and living standards.
 
• It uses 10 indicators including nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.
 
• The index provides a more nuanced understanding of poverty beyond income-based measures.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established to replace the Planning Commission.
 
• It aims to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states on a continuous basis.
 
 
 
• **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)**
 
 
• OPHI is an economic research centre within the University of Oxford.
 
• It develops and implements multidimensional approaches to measuring poverty and wellbeing.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**
 
 
• UNDP is the United Nations' global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life.
 
• It works in nearly 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion.
